dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.confirm_: I would gladly join your colony! As provisions, I'll need %sx %s. Do we have a deal?
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.main: Hello traveler! It's good to see a friendly face. How can I help you?
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.skills_i: I have the following skills to offer:
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_1: I hid in an old cave for days... The hordes out there are getting more aggressive by the day.
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_2: My old camp was ambushed. I'm the only one who made it here.
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_3: I wandered through the wilderness for weeks, always searching for a safe settlement.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.done: A good trade. Take care out there.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.empty: I currently have absolutely nothing in my backpack that I could spare.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.haggle_acc: %sx %s? Yes, that's a fair trade. Let's do business.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.haggle_rej: Only %sx %s? That's not enough. I need more of that.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.has_items: This is what I've gathered on my travels. What do you need?
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.player_emp: You don't have anything on you that would be worth a fair trade.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.player_off: So you want my %s? Okay, what will you give me in return?
gui.survivorcolonies.recruit.subtitle: §8Lone Survivor
gui.survivorcolonies.recruit.title: Survivor
gui.survivorcolonies.trade.subtitle: §8Trade & Barter
gui.survivorcolonies.trade.title: Survivor - Trade
survivor.text.000001: Don't look at me like I need you; just keep your distance and stay out of my way.
survivor.text.000002: Don't talk about trusting me; just prove you can survive until sunrise without needing my help.
survivor.text.000003: Don't get any ideas; I'll take whatever help you offer and still keep my distance.
survivor.text.000004: Fine, if you keep doing what you're doing, maybe I won't have to worry about scavenging for scraps again.
survivor.text.000005: Well, if we just keep working together and stay close to the fire, I bet things will work out perfectly!
survivor.text.000006: We could totally work together, I guess, as long as we keep our distance and you promise to share all your really good snacks!
survivor.text.000007: I hope you found what you needed; building things together always makes surviving feel like a picnic!
survivor.text.000008: I'm happy to help with anything you need, just tell me where we should start!
survivor.text.000009: I'll give you space; I just want you to know I'm here if you change your mind.
survivor.text.000011: Got it. I wasn't going to bother you anyway.
survivor.text.000012: I won't talk about trust; I'm focused on making sure we see the sunrise.
survivor.text.000013: What happens if I actually need help?
survivor.text.000014: I don't need your permission to survive
survivor.text.000015: I respect that. We can keep it strictly practical then.
survivor.text.000016: What makes you so sure about keeping your distance?
survivor.text.000018: I hope you find better than scraps soon
survivor.text.000019: What kind of things are you talking about?
survivor.text.000020: Oh, really? And what makes you think that's actually going to happen?
survivor.text.000021: We'll make it work. Just keep us focused on the fire.
survivor.text.000022: What exactly do you mean by 'work out perfectly'?
survivor.text.000024: Sounds like a plan. Distance and snacks it is!
survivor.text.000025: What exactly does "keep our distance" mean in this context?
survivor.text.000028: A picnic? You sound awfully cheerful for someone who's seen what we've been through.
survivor.text.000029: Don't sound so happy about it; we barely survived.
survivor.text.000030: Let's start by reviewing the map and figuring out our priorities.
survivor.text.000031: What do you think would be the most effective place to begin?
survivor.text.000033: Is it always this foggy out here, or did something just change with the wind?
survivor.text.000034: You think I'm going to cry over it, but when you see old man Hemlock, you remember what it was like to lose everything in one burn.
survivor.text.000035: You seem capable enough, so if you don't mind me asking, what exactly are we trying to build here?
survivor.text.000036: You talk about trust like it's something you just build with wood and stone; it's earned in blood, kid.
survivor.text.000037: I suppose we could call this 'gathering resources' rather than 'scavenging for basic caloric inputs,' couldn't we?
survivor.text.000038: The local flora seems unusually vibrant after the rain; I wonder what catalyst caused that color shift.
survivor.text.000039: I spent years studying complex systems, but I realized the most fascinating structure is always a thriving community like ours.
survivor.text.000040: I left everything behind for a chance to belong somewhere else.
survivor.text.000041: Hey, did you manage to get any good fishing hauls today? I heard there are some rare glow squid near these coordinates!
survivor.text.000042: We can survive together, maybe, but don't assume that means anything other than temporary convenience.
survivor.text.000043: They say running doesn't erase what you left behind.
survivor.text.000044: Did you know that arranging these mushrooms like this actually increases their nutrient absorption rate by about three percent?
survivor.text.000045: I hope you don't mind me asking where you got those nice boots; they really suit your... I mean, yours.
survivor.text.000046: Don't worry about it! We just need enough coal for tonight and we'll figure out how to make everything perfect again, I promise!
survivor.text.000047: Oh gosh, analyzing your behavioral data suggests a 78% probability that we can cooperate, provided you pass my little ethical algorithm!
survivor.text.000048: Did you happen to notice how disproportionately loud that creeper was, or are we still discussing the optimal ratio of dirt to wood for casual conversation?
survivor.text.000049: I've always been more interested in *how* things work than *why*, which is probably why I ended up wandering out here in the first place.
survivor.text.000050: If we build this shelter together, I know we'll be safe from anything the night throws at us.
survivor.text.000051: If we pool our knowledge together, I think we can optimize this entire settlement to thrive.
survivor.text.000052: Just because you *say* you trust me doesn't mean you've earned the right to stand in my light.
survivor.text.000053: It's funny, all this building reminds me of the biggest market stalls I ever saw—it just means we can build something wonderful together!
survivor.text.000054: If you keep your word, I swear I'll stand by you until everything we need is safe.
survivor.text.000055: If we're going to look into this, I need you to keep your back to the shadows because something out there doesn't seem comfortable with us being here.
survivor.text.000056: Are you absolutely sure this path is safe, because I just keep seeing shadows and I don't know where they came from?
survivor.text.000057: If we don't work perfectly together, I honestly don't know what we'll do when the night falls.
survivor.text.000058: The strength of this camp is simply the certainty that we will face what comes next together.
survivor.text.000059: They said you were just a stray dog, but I know what you really are—you're everything that took them from me.
survivor.text.000060: Do you really think discussing local flora counts as stimulating conversation?
survivor.text.000061: Are we absolutely certain that this resource allocation model accounts for potential behavioral deviations under stress?
survivor.text.000062: I've spent so many years analyzing the failures of the system that I finally understand exactly how to make sure no one ever gets away with anything again.
survivor.text.000063: Good day! Hope you’ve managed to find some decent berries; we should organize a foraging route soon!
survivor.text.000064: If you don't trust me, then explain the logic behind your doubt.
survivor.text.000065: Just keep your distance, but don't wander off—I really don't have the energy to clean up a mess all over again.
survivor.text.000066: Looks like you've got your corner sorted out—now all we need is a good dinner plan for everyone!
survivor.text.000067: I used to haggle over rare dyes and enchanted tools; this whole 'scavenge berries until you drop' gig is quite the downgrade.
survivor.text.000068: I keep running simulations, and every variable seems to predict some form of inevitable betrayal.
survivor.text.000069: This sunset is perfect for checking traps and figuring out what we should raid tomorrow.
survivor.text.000070: Wow, look at all those strange little plants; I wonder if they taste as good as the berries back home.
survivor.text.000071: Did you find any extra planks while you were exploring?
survivor.text.000072: The way the sun hits those wheat fields makes me wonder how much energy they actually store.
survivor.text.000073: You haven't shown me anything yet, so I can't tell you what to believe.
survivor.text.000074: Don't get any ideas that this sudden willingness to help means you can just walk all over me again.
survivor.text.000075: If you think this is foolproof, you clearly haven't accounted for the sheer statistical improbability of human incompetence.
survivor.text.000076: I know I haven't earned it yet, but please just let me help with anything you need.
survivor.text.000077: Don't look at me like I expect you to suddenly feel safe; your history speaks louder than any words you might offer.
survivor.text.000078: I used to be good at spotting danger from miles away—skills that are definitely coming in handy out here.
survivor.text.000079: Those mushrooms are quite striking; do they make any sort of delicious stew?
survivor.text.000080: Honestly, your survival rate has been acceptably high so far, which means I suppose your usefulness hasn't peaked yet.
survivor.text.000081: Just because you're offering help doesn't mean you know anything about what I've survived.
survivor.text.000082: If you can't prove you won't leave me here to face whatever is out there, then we really shouldn't be working together.
survivor.text.000083: The sunset looks perfect for gathering firewood tonight, don't you think?
survivor.text.000084: Don't assume I need your kind help; I just appreciate knowing how easily you break.
survivor.text.000085: Show me the data proving your usefulness, or frankly, I don't see how we survive if you keep acting like an unpredictable variable.
survivor.text.000086: I wonder if we could get those carrots to grow even bigger just by adjusting the humidity in this little corner?
survivor.text.000087: Don't get any ideas; I wasn't looking for a family, just somewhere to crash until the next place called to me.
survivor.text.000088: It’s genuinely disappointing how little evidence-based reasoning you employed when you dismantled my entire life's work, all under the guise of 'accidental negligence.'
survivor.text.000089: I've done some research on this biome; maybe we can work together to optimize our chances of survival here.
survivor.text.000090: I just... I really hope my research is good enough this time to finally make amends for everything that went wrong before.
survivor.text.000091: I really hope you can trust me, because breaking your heart would just make things much harder on both of us.
survivor.text.000092: Just keep up; you think *your* scavenging trips are rough? You haven't seen a real firefight since you were knee-high to a creeper.
survivor.text.000093: A strong settlement isn't built on iron or diamonds; it's built on trust, and I know a reliable partnership when I see one.
survivor.text.000094: They stole my research and they left me with nothing but this festering need to see them pay.
survivor.text.000095: The wood on this frame seems strong enough to last through another season.
survivor.text.000096: If I survive this lovely little homestead with you, I fully intend to use all the stories as leverage later.
survivor.text.000097: Must we talk about the weather, or is this just how pathetic small talk always has to be around here?
survivor.text.000098: The only thing that kept me going was remembering how they took everything from us.
survivor.text.000099: Wow, these pumpkins really look like they're going to put on a spectacular feast this year!
survivor.text.000100: Looks like we all worked hard today; maybe there's time for a nice meal before nightfall?
survivor.text.000101: I've got your back, but even the friendliest corner of this world can hide something that smells suspiciously like trouble.
survivor.text.000102: I'm sure we can make up a story that makes me seem less like I ran away from everything.
survivor.text.000103: Don't expect me to share anything just because you built a nice fence; I've learned that kindness is always temporary around here.
survivor.text.000104: Do you think there's any measurable difference in crop yield when planting seeds near flowing water?
survivor.text.000105: It looks like you've got some great roots going there; I bet those crops will yield enough for a proper feast!
survivor.text.000106: Maybe if we started by mapping out the best crops, we could build up some shared data points?
survivor.text.000107: Wow, look at those mushrooms—I bet they taste sweet after a good rain!
survivor.text.000108: Well, look at you; hope whatever trinkets you found today were worth my time!
survivor.text.000109: The river hasn't changed course much since I was last passing through.
survivor.text.000110: If we've survived this far side-by-side, I suspect you understand that trust isn't a feeling; it's just another resource we manage.
survivor.text.000111: Don't just stand there; if you want to chat, fine, but don't expect me to suddenly start caring about your day.
survivor.text.000112: My research gave me the knowledge to ruin things once, but I'm finally here, hoping to rebuild enough of anything good that I can ever find my way back into grace.
survivor.text.000113: Looks like you found some good kindling; we should probably stack more before the evening rain hits.
survivor.text.000114: I don't know if I can even trust anyone around here; everyone just seems to be waiting for something awful to happen.
survivor.text.000115: It wasn't anything important, I just needed to disappear before they found me.
survivor.text.000116: I suppose your continued existence has yielded enough predictable data points to warrant my limited cooperation.
survivor.text.000117: Figure out why I left? Oh, you want the juicy details of my spectacular failure at life, do you?
survivor.text.000118: You'd better have empirical data for that claim, or I'm assuming it's pure anecdotal fallacy.
survivor.text.000119: Do you ever wonder what happened to things... or people... that just vanished?
survivor.text.000120: Oh look, you remembered how to breathe; what riveting piece of small talk did you have planned for me today?
survivor.text.000121: What do you seek out here?
survivor.text.000122: Just tell me what you think we should do next, but please don't pretend that your answer is actually helpful.
survivor.text.000123: Don't expect me to be your friend just because we share a meal; keep your distance and watch your back.
survivor.text.000124: Wow, look at those mushrooms; I wonder what kind of spores they actually release when it rains.
survivor.text.000125: I just hope that being useful enough to finally belong here means I'll never have to worry about getting scammed out of my entire life savings again.
survivor.text.000126: Just keep your distance and don't ask questions; I survived enough to know that asking too many questions gets you killed out here.
survivor.text.000127: I... I cannot calculate a reliable outcome from that input; your motives remain statistically volatile.
survivor.text.000128: Don't mistake my silence for weakness; I only see obstacles and exits.
survivor.text.000129: Honestly, I used to think the best way to survive was having twenty men and a tactical advantage, but now it's just good shoveling technique!
survivor.text.000130: The sun is out today, which means we have a decent chance to gather some extra firewood before the rain comes.
survivor.text.000131: I know things might feel uncertain right now, but I'll wait until you decide if we can build something good together.
survivor.text.000132: Don't mistake my tolerance for anything resembling faith; your assumed reliability is statistically irrelevant.
survivor.text.000133: If you want me to believe you, you'll have to show it with more than just words.
survivor.text.000134: You know, for someone who seems so relaxed, you haven't even bothered to check your six yet.
survivor.text.000135: I've spent enough time studying failing civilizations to know that your suspicion is statistically predictable.
survivor.text.000136: We move together because the alternative is worse.
survivor.text.000137: You think starvation is scary; you haven't seen a man with nothing left to lose and nowhere to run.
survivor.text.000138: Honestly, for a peaceful little settlement, we've managed to avoid any actual conflict this week; I’m starting to worry about your combat readiness skills.
survivor.text.000139: I just... I don't know where else to go, but if we can all stick together, maybe it will feel like home again.
survivor.text.000140: I knew we were meant to be; nothing beats a good partnership and an even better sense of destiny!
survivor.text.000141: I'm happy to help, but you need to understand that earning my trust is going to take a lot more than just a few kind words.
survivor.text.000142: Don't get any ideas; I haven't forgotten what was taken from me, so keep your distance.
survivor.text.000143: Why do you always stare at the horizon like nothing interesting is going to happen out there?
survivor.text.000144: The silence where my family used to be is the only thing keeping me focused enough to find them again.
survivor.text.000145: The humidity here is surprisingly high for an established settlement.
survivor.text.000146: You think trust is something you just 'give'? It's a commodity, and right now, your credit rating is non-existent.
survivor.text.000147: The weather today is fascinating—I wonder if the humidity levels correlate with local crop yields?
survivor.text.000148: I just... I keep expecting to hear orders again, which makes me jump every time someone moves too fast.
survivor.text.000149: You really think survival is about finding enough diamonds, don't you?
survivor.text.000150: The sun is actually out today; we should try fishing on that stream before it gets too chilly.
survivor.text.000151: We might not know everything right now, but I bet we can make something amazing if we just keep working together.
survivor.text.000152: Predictable contribution is far more valuable to the colony than any promise of loyalty.
survivor.text.000153: If you truly believe in this, then we have no choice but to proceed exactly as planned, because I can't bear the thought of everything falling apart again.
survivor.text.000154: My old life felt too much like reading from a book, so I ran until I could write my own story in the dirt.
survivor.text.000155: I just want to find a way to make things right for them.
survivor.text.000156: I don't remember a life before I started running.
survivor.text.000157: You think that means anything? I've seen promises like yours before, and they always turn to dust.
survivor.text.000158: Don't get cocky; I still remember what it feels like when you can't breathe and everything around you is trying to kill you.
survivor.text.000159: Fine, I'll tell you what I think, but don't expect me to like it; your intentions are still murky enough for coin toss.
survivor.text.000160: The way you've organized those storage crates is remarkably efficient; I wonder what principles of physics govern optimal spatial arrangement?
survivor.text.000161: Fine, what do you want to talk about? Just keep it quick and don't expect me to care.
survivor.text.000162: I never thought I'd be building a peaceful life like this, but maybe that's where my war ends and my real journey begins.
survivor.text.000163: Oh, you're still wearing those suspiciously unblemished boots? You must have found them in a very rich grave site.
survivor.text.000164: Is it normal that the wheat seems... brighter today?
survivor.text.000165: You know, if you polish your copper ingots enough, they actually look almost as nice as the gold I used to trade with back in my day.
survivor.text.000166: I learned early that nothing lasts if you rely on anyone else.
survivor.text.000167: I wonder if I could breed a glowstone that also produces perfectly ripe wheat!
survivor.text.000168: If we keep talking about this, are you sure there isn't some trap I haven't seen yet?
survivor.text.000169: Just keep your distance for now; it'll be easier if we don't talk about anything important.
survivor.text.000170: You really think gold coins are going to fix what you cost me, after all those years?
survivor.text.000171: The air is clearer here than I expected; you should try walking toward the ridge at sunset.
survivor.text.000172: Don't look at me like that; it's hardly remarkable how quickly you managed to burn those rations.
survivor.text.000173: I just... I don't understand how this biome got so far from any known research site.
survivor.text.000174: I'm sure we can work through this, just tell me what you need from me to feel safe again.
survivor.text.000175: It was the unstable geothermal flux that forced me to abandon my old lab—and frankly, you shouldn't touch anything until I tell you how it works.
survivor.text.000176: Look, I appreciate the vote of confidence, but if we survive this, assume everything—including your promises—is subject to a steep discount.
survivor.text.000177: The sun is out today; I hope you found something edible in the woods.
survivor.text.000178: I learned that brute force only wins until something stronger shows up.
survivor.text.000179: Show me consistency over time; reputation means nothing when the night falls.
survivor.text.000180: If you are here, then maybe... maybe this time I actually won't mess up the calculations.
survivor.text.000181: Why do you keep looking at the river? Because if I knew what happened to them, maybe this pointless wandering wouldn't be all there is left.
survivor.text.000182: I understand if you’re still analyzing my motives, but even a small variable of cooperation helps us all survive this biome change
survivor.text.000183: The data suggests that paranoia is a resource drain; we need cooperation, not suspicion.
survivor.text.000184: Oh, you trust me? Fascinating data point—I should probably run some risk assessment on your emotional stability before I proceed.
survivor.text.000185: What exactly are you hoping to learn by wasting my time with pointless chatter?
survivor.text.000186: You know, for someone who spent three hours mining cobblestone, you seem remarkably unbored.
survivor.text.000187: Don't mistake my silence for weakness; you just haven't seen me angry enough yet.
survivor.text.000188: Maybe we don't know each other yet, but I promise I only trade in good intentions and useful goods.
survivor.text.000189: I know we can build anything here, as long as you keep your back pressed right up against mine!
survivor.text.000190: Honestly, I once traded entire stacks of obsidian for nothing but a half-eaten loaf of bread—you have no idea what other nonsense passes for currency out here.
survivor.text.000191: I never meant for things to get this bad again; I just want to earn my keep and help build something real with all of you.
survivor.text.000192: The sunset really makes this valley look like it was painted just for us.
survivor.text.000193: Don't mistake my silence for cooperation; I only tolerate your presence because you haven't managed to irritate me yet.
survivor.text.000194: I don't know how long I can stay here, but please just tell me what to do next so I don't mess anything up again.
survivor.text.000195: Trust is not given; it is earned through shared burden, and we survive by carrying that weight together.
survivor.text.000196: Don't expect me to share rations based on handshake agreements; I still haven't seen your combat record.
survivor.text.000197: Oh, um, so you actually managed to grow wheat this far north? I was just wondering how... if the soil composition here is okay enough for anything at all.
survivor.text.000198: Is it... is it normal that the stars look so much closer from out here?
survivor.text.000199: I never understood why I had to leave; it was simply the air that pulled me away from everything familiar.
survivor.text.000200: Are you sure this isn't some kind of trap?
survivor.text.000201: The rain slowed enough to actually make moving around bearable.
survivor.text.000202: I hope we have enough extra bread because I'm really worried about running out of anything at all.
survivor.text.000203: Don't expect me to discuss anything pleasant; perhaps you could explain the flawed thermal dynamics of that ridiculously inefficient fire pit?
survivor.text.000204: I’ve seen worse than a few misplaced tools; we build this together, starting now.
survivor.text.000205: I just... I don't know how to trade anymore; all I can do is panic and gather wood.
survivor.text.000206: Do you think... if we figured out how to reliably power that generator, would the value of all our other stored goods actually go up?
survivor.text.000207: I need to see you contribute before I consider this anything beyond a temporary alliance.
survivor.text.000208: I'm sure we can build something amazing if you just keep showing up and doing your part!
survivor.text.000209: You seem awfully comfortable standing right there in that patch of weeds; isn't it ridiculous?
survivor.text.000210: You want me to trust you, do you? You should probably start by paying for the privilege.
survivor.text.000211: You wouldn't believe the strange treasures I stumbled upon just from wandering between market stalls!
survivor.text.000212: Oh, look who managed to crawl out of their hole; don't worry, I brought snacks and questionable life advice.
survivor.text.000213: Oh, look at you, thinking I might actually care about your survival skills; bless your optimistic little heart.
survivor.text.000214: I only traded with people I knew could actually keep their end of a deal.
survivor.text.000215: I'll trade you my knowledge for your company, but don't think I forgot how to bargain.
survivor.text.000216: Our continued operation depends entirely on maintaining this equilibrium we have established.
survivor.text.000217: Are you sure we really need to build the lumber mill right here by the river? I just... I keep wondering what kind of rare goods might be further inland instead.
survivor.text.000218: The data suggests that trust itself is merely a temporary variable in our current equation.
survivor.text.000219: Another day, another pile of lumber—if you’re going to complain about it, at least make sure you hauled the damn wood yourself.
survivor.text.000220: Well, if we're going to play this cooperation game, you better be ready for everything I throw at you!
survivor.text.000221: Oh gosh, you want to talk 'trust'? Well, that's cute! Let's just say I appreciate the *idea* of it, as long as we both remember who was there first!
survivor.text.000222: Don't make me worry about this again; we need everyone working together if we want to see another sunrise.
survivor.text.000223: You better not mess this up, because if I have to rely on your 'good intentions' again, I might actually lose my appetite for people.
survivor.text.000224: Just try to keep the small talk brief; I've got enough things to figure out without forced pleasantries.
survivor.text.000225: I still don't like this, but if you insist on telling me what I should be curious about, fine.
survivor.text.000226: The data suggests your survival is fundamentally unstable.
survivor.text.000227: I just hope that everything we build together will be enough to keep this trust safe forever.
survivor.text.000228: Do you... do you think the sun sets in the same spot every night, or should I maybe keep checking?
survivor.text.000229: Do you think this strange patch of grass is edible, or should I just leave it alone because I don't want to risk poisoning myself again?
